en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Thirteenth Chapter
Regarding the discourse on presence:
Is it the case that one who is present abandons the fetters?
Yes, it is.
"One who is lustful abandons lust; one who is hateful abandons hatred; one who is deluded abandons delusion; one who is defiled abandons the defilements"?

One should not say this... [and so on] ... "One abandons lust by means of lust; one abandons hatred by means of hatred; one abandons delusion by means of delusion; one abandons the defilements by means of the defilements"?
It should not be said thus ...
[and so on] ... Is lust associated with consciousness? Is the Path associated with consciousness? Yes.
Is there a convergence of two contacts …pe… of two consciousnesses?
One should not say so …pe…
Lust is unwholesome; the Path is wholesome.

[If this is] so, then do wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, inferior and superior states, dark and bright counterparts, come into manifestation? [If you say] yes, then [you must admit that] they do. But is it not the case that these states are mutually exclusive? Therefore, your position is untenable.
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Do wholesome and unwholesome states come into manifestation?
“Yes, [it is so].
“Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
‘Bhikkhus, these four things are exceedingly far apart’?”
Which four? The sky and the earth, monks—
this is the first pair that is very far apart … [as before] … Therefore, the Dhamma of the virtuous is far from those who are wicked.”
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said—
“Wholesome and unwholesome [states] ...pe...
come into manifestation. Does one who has brought them into manifestation abandon the fetters?
“Yes.
“But was it not said by the Blessed One:
‘When his mind is thus concentrated... [and so forth]?”
“He inclines his mind toward the knowledge of the destruction of the taints.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
Therefore, it should not be said that "one who is present abandons the fetter.
It should not be said.
“Does one who has brought [the path] face-to-face abandon the fetter?”—
“Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Thus knowing and thus seeing, his mind is liberated from the influx of sensual desire …pe… his mind is liberated even from the influx of ignorance.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes, [it is so].
“In that case, one who has brought [the defilement] face-to-face abandons the fetter.
The Discussion on What is Face-to-Face is finished.
